_comment: cherrypick orchestration config. Copy to config.json and adjust. A module is located by 'path' (relative to this file's directory — in the monorepo every module ships in the same checkout) or, for an out-of-tree module, a 'repo' URL cloned by `cherrypick install` into ~/.cherrypick/modules/<repo-name>. Never hardcode absolute machine paths.
_home_note: Runtime home (this config.json, logs/, state/, dashboard.html) = CHERRYPICK_HOME if set, else the repo root in a source checkout, else ~/.cherrypick for a pip-installed copy. An installed copy thus reads ~/.cherrypick/config.json.
_modules_home_note: Managed module checkouts live under CHERRYPICK_MODULES_HOME, else CHERRYPICK_HOME/modules, else ~/.cherrypick/modules. `install` clones a module only when its checkout is absent and never touches an existing one; `uninstall` leaves checkouts in place.
_capabilities_note: What this machine has, written by the installer (run.py capabilities --detect --write) and editable by hand. claude: the Claude Code CLI, which the advisor and the EOD/morning narratives shell out to. dolt: a running Dolt server with the earnings, options and stocks clones, which the earnings module and the technicals report read. Absent or false means every feature that needs it is off and hidden from the console, whatever its own switch says.

meic._path_note: Locate the module by 'path' (absolute or relative to this file). In the monorepo every module ships in the same checkout, so the relative path is the way; a 'repo' clone URL is still honored for an out-of-tree module, but the pre-monorepo split-repo URLs were removed 2026-07-29 so a path miss can never clone retired code.
meic._keyring_note: The module's OS-keyring service name, used by `cherrypick account`/`connect` to read/select the module's live-trading account (ACCOUNT_NUMBER) via the shared CredentialStore. Optional 'keyring_legacy_services' lists read-only fallbacks (MEIC keeps 'tastytrade-mcp' for pre-rename creds). Omit to disable account selection for this module.
meic._live_db_note: Phase-5 seam: the module's LIVE-trades ledger, read ONLY by the explicitly live-tagged surfaces (`cherrypick report --live`). Deliberately a separate key from paper.paper_db — calibrate and every promotion reading go through the paper path and can never see this file. Same resolution rules as paper_db (absolute / ~-expanded / module-root relative).
meic._live_note: 2026-10-14, the flies/bwb posture: the supervisor's meic-live job runs one `cherrypick.meic.live_loop --once --live` tick a minute ONLY while today's arm record (written by /live-meic-start after a literal YES) is valid; the tick self-disarms past the module's own live.disarm_time and the watchdog backstops at disarm_time + grace. The module's enable_live_trading stays its master switch.

live._notify_trades_note: LIVE fills, stops and exits from meic_trades.db through the meic_ic adapter, relabelled LIVE with a desktop toast (trade_notifier._LiveNotifier). A pending entry is announced once the broker confirms it. Known limit: a later IC recorded while an earlier one is still pending moves the entry watermark past it, so that earlier fill goes unannounced -- unreachable at max_structures_per_day 1.

paper._tick_interval_note: Supervisor cadence for the paper tick: the daemon spawns tick_argv (default: once_argv minus --force) every N seconds. 60 halves the old hardcoded 2-minute schtasks cadence (2026-08-09 supervisor cutover) for tighter exit management on open condors. At >= 60 this is a short-lived tick job; BELOW 60 the shape changes -- see the flies block's resident_start/resident_end note. `task_name` is the only legacy-schtasks key still read (tasks.legacy_task_names deletes the pre-cutover task by that name); the module's own --install-task remains for standalone use but the orchestrator never invokes it, which is why there is no install_argv/uninstall_argv here.
paper._tick_on_non_trading_days_note: OPTIONAL, default false. A tick of 60s or more runs on trading days only (2026-10-12): no spawn-per-tick module had ever written a ledger row on a weekend or holiday. Set true for a module whose tick must run every day. Overnight on a trading day is never gated.
paper._tick_argv_note: OPTIONAL. The exact argv the supervisor spawns each tick. Omit it and the orchestrator derives one from once_argv by dropping --force, which is what every module here relies on; set it only when a module's tick must differ from its manual one-shot.
paper._settlement_check_note: Enabled 2026-08-26, last of the paper modules. It was off because the check reads session_settled/positions_today from a module's own --status and meic's reported neither, so turning it on alone would have been a check that could not fire. It matters more now that paper.evaluate_open_trade REFUSES to settle a position with no underlying price rather than booking it at zero intrinsic: the right failure, but a silent one, since the position simply stays open.
paper._regime_cuts_note: Nightly regime-cuts artifact (2026-09-19): at regime_cuts_at (ET, trading days) the supervisor runs regime_cuts_argv, which writes data/<module>/regime_cuts-<session>.json plus the latest copy that the console's regime slide and the advisor's deep pack read. 16:40 sits after the module settles and after review-provisional (16:30) and before advisor deep_at (17:00); a deep_at earlier than this reads last night's artifact, which the pack labels stale. Remove both keys to drop the job.
paper._fee_reconcile_note: Broker fee reconciliation of settled LIVE ICs (2026-10-15), the job flies and bwb run, and unconditional on arming for the same reason: a session traded on a day that was never followed by an armed one must still be confirmed. At fee_reconcile_at (ET, trading days) the supervisor runs fee_reconcile_argv, which matches each settled live row's broker order ids and settlement lines and, with --apply, replaces the ledger's modeled fees and settlement_fees with the broker's (the modeled values kept once in fee_reconciliations). The gross is reported, never rewritten. Without --apply it only reports. No --symbol: it reconciles whatever symbol each pending row traded, since the live loop's pinned symbol can change. 09:25 is after the broker posts the prior session's settlement lines and clear of flies (09:15) and bwb (09:20). Needs the module's broker credentials (GET-only). Remove both keys to drop the job.
paper._paper_db_note: Path to the module's paper-trades SQLite DB — MUST point at the file the module actually WRITES (a mismatch silently blinds the orchestrator's report/reconcile/dashboard and the watchdog freshness check). Relative resolves against the module checkout; a leading '~' or env var expands (use e.g. '~/.cherrypick/data/meic/paper_trades.db' when the module keeps its data in the managed home); an absolute path is used as-is.

calibration._comment: Optional. `cherrypick calibrate` reads paper P&L per profile and advises whether a qualified challenger should replace the live 'champion' (advisory only; never switches live risk). 'champion' names the currently-live profile -- every other tag observed is a challenger compared against it on return_on_capital (falling back to net_pnl). Omit 'champion' entirely to get per-tag qualification readings with NO champion/challenger comparison (for a module whose tags are parallel experiments rather than a risk sequence -- see flies below). 'deliberate_only' tags are never auto-recommended even if they qualify and beat the champion; 'rule' overrides the default {min_sessions:14 (older configs' min_days is still read), min_win_rate:0.6, min_sample:20} and may add 'margin' (default 0.0 -- any positive edge counts as beating the champion).
calibration._arms_cutover_note: Updated 2026-08-07 for the arms cutover (config.risk.json's _arms_cutover_note): champion is now `control` (today's deployed policy, formerly `conservative` -- same values, new name). The retired ladder/GEX tags (conservative/moderate/aggressive/very-aggressive/gex-open/gex-blocked) never write a new row again, so they simply stop appearing as challengers going forward; their historical rows stay under their own tag and never blend into `control`'s reading, since the tag NAME itself is what segregates the eras here -- no data_epoch needed (that key is suite-wide and would also truncate flies/earnings' unrelated history). `open` is deliberate_only: it runs with per_side_stop_management OFF (held to settlement/force-close, no per-side stop at all), a materially different risk posture from control's canonical MEIC+ stop, not just a quality-gate relaxation -- qualifying on paper should not auto-promote a no-stop policy without a human decision, the same reasoning very-aggressive's deliberate_only carried.
calibration._retired_2026_08_20: The champion/challenger comparison this block drove is RETIRED. Judging arms belongs to packages/advisor's experiments now -- one mechanism rather than two answering the same question on different evidence and different thresholds. `cherrypick calibrate` still reports the per-tag READING and its qualification checks. 'champion', 'deliberate_only' and rule.'margin' are now read without error and have NO effect; left here so an existing config keeps loading, and safe to delete.

flies._comment: cherrypick-flies: 0DTE net-credit butterflies ('profit forest'), paper only, XSP (SPX through 2026-07-28). Reads the shared stream cache READ-ONLY and runs no streamer of its own, so it REQUIRES the suite's streamer to be running and subscribed to its symbol. ENABLED, but it has still never completed a live session — watch the first one, in particular the quote_stats line in the log (which separates 'the streamer gave us nothing' from 'the strategy found nothing') and the arm_divergence figure (if the arms agree nearly always, the comparison cannot answer anything and max_center_distance_pct is the first thing to revisit).
flies._broker_note: Live-scaffold onboarding (docs/live-trading-plan.md in the module): flies has no tt.py, so its config-declared broker/credential CLI is broker_cli.py; `cherrypick connect/account --module flies` drive it exactly like MEIC's tt.py. keyring service fliesagent; live_db is the SEPARATE live ledger read only by `report --live` (never by calibrate/promotion).
flies._live_note: Watchdog + notification wiring for the module's LIVE loop (the module itself owns arming/trading; this block only tells the orchestrator how to WATCH it). task_name is the module's self-registered live task; the loop self-disarms at the module's live.disarm_time (arming is per-day) and disarm_time/disarm_grace_minutes here are the watchdog's BACKSTOP window — past it, a still-registered live task means self-disarm failed, so the watchdog sets the suite halt flag (risk-reducing only; it never touches the task) and raises CRITICAL. notify_trades pushes live entries/completions/settlements from live_db with a hard-to-miss LIVE prefix + desktop toast, from the notifier path (never the trading loop).

live._tick_argv_note: OPTIONAL. The argv the supervisor's <module>-live job spawns each tick while the module is armed. Omitted here because the orchestrator derives it the same way it does for paper; set it only if the live tick must differ.

paper._kind_note: self_healing, NOT cherrypick_scheduled. This was cherrypick_scheduled, which registers one entry task at entry_time and one exit task at exit_time — a shape that fits Earnings (one entry, one exit per day) and is wrong for a legged 0DTE strategy. A single daily entry would open a credit spread at noon and never look at it again, so the completing spread could never be bought and the completion rate — the module's headline measurement — would read 0% every day for reasons that have nothing to do with the market. cherrypick_scheduled also hardcodes the earnings launcher verbs, so this module's own entry_argv would have been ignored entirely.
paper._timing_note: tick_interval_seconds is the supervisor cadence. Sub-minute (<60) runs the module's own resident `--interval N` loop IN-SESSION (the resident_start/resident_end window below, supervised: restarted on death and on silence_seconds of log silence) plus a 60s `--once` spawn job OUTSIDE that window, so settlement at 16:20, retry-until-settled, and the hourly idle heartbeat keep exactly the shape the 1-minute task gave them. 15s (2026-08-09 supervisor cutover, was 60 -- the OS scheduler's floor) samples transient completion-debit dips ~4x finer; the completion rate is NOT comparable across that date (any discrete poll understates what a resting limit order would catch, so faster polling measures a truer, higher rate). The change is journaled in the module's decision journal and its CLAUDE.md. `task_name` is the only legacy-schtasks key still read, for deleting the pre-cutover task by name.
paper._resident_window_note: OPTIONAL, and only meaningful when tick_interval_seconds < 60: the ET window inside which the resident loop runs, on trading days. Defaults 09:30/16:00. These gate the ENTIRE resident job -- widen them and the loop runs longer, narrow them and it simply will not run outside -- so they are worth stating explicitly rather than inheriting silently. Outside the window the 60s `--once` job takes over (that is what settles at 16:20).
paper._once_note: No --force. --force bypasses the RTH gate AND the trading-day gate, the second of which exists to stop a Saturday tick from 'settling' a session that never happened and emitting a paper-eod-<saturday>.md the suite digest would ingest as real. The module's own --install-task registers plain `--once`, so --force here would also mean the orchestrator drives the loop differently from its own scheduled task.
paper._regime_cuts_note: Nightly regime-cuts artifact (2026-09-19): at regime_cuts_at (ET, trading days) the supervisor runs regime_cuts_argv, which writes data/<module>/regime_cuts-<session>.json plus the latest copy that the console's regime slide and the advisor's deep pack read. 16:40 sits after the module settles and after review-provisional (16:30) and before advisor deep_at (17:00); a deep_at earlier than this reads last night's artifact, which the pack labels stale. Remove both keys to drop the job.
paper._selector_fit_note: The flies selector arm's nightly model (2026-10-04): at selector_fit_at (ET, trading days) the supervisor runs selector_fit_argv, which fits the model for the NEXT session from every settled row before it and writes data/flies/selector_model-<session>.json; the paper loop pins it at that session's first tick. 16:45 sits after the 16:40 cuts. A no-op that says so while no `selector` arm is declared in the flies config. Catches up until midnight only: a missed night means one session run as control's twin, which the choice record names. Remove both keys to drop the job.
paper._fee_reconcile_note: Broker-cash reconciliation of settled LIVE sessions (2026-09-22): at fee_reconcile_at (ET, trading days) the supervisor runs fee_reconcile_argv, which re-derives net/fees/gross_pnl/pnl for each settled live position from the broker's own transactions and snapshots the modeled values into modeled_* first. UNCONDITIONAL ON ARMING, which is the point: this used to ride the live tick, where it ran only under --live, sat behind the dead-man's switch, and stopped entirely once the loop disarmed -- so a session traded on Tuesday went unreconciled forever if Wednesday was never armed. 09:15 is after the broker posts the prior session's settlement lines overnight and before the entry window opens. Needs the module's broker credentials (GET-only). Remove both keys to drop the job.
paper._settlement_check_note: Opt in the watchdog's settlement-overdue alert: past the settle time + retry buffer on a trading day it reads this module's --status and WARNs if session_settled is false with positions_today > 0 (a settle stuck on a stale feed, which the freshness check misses because the loop is still running). Only set for a module whose --status reports session_settled/positions_today (flies does). settlement_grace_minutes is minutes AFTER the 16:00 close before 'overdue' applies -- it must cover the module's own settle time (flies settles at 16:20) plus a few retries, or it false-alarms every day in the 16:00-settle window. Default 30 (fires at 16:30).

calibration._comment: These tags are parallel experiment arms (control/gex/time_window/width-N), not a risk sequence -- there is no currently-live 'champion' among them, so no 'champion' key is set: cherrypick calibrate produces per-arm qualification readings with NO champion/challenger recommendation. width-2..width-5 and width-10 are the wing-width sweep, pinned in STRIKE increments via wing_width_strikes (control at the default width is its 1-strike rung); wide_wing is the retired SPX-era single-point width arm, listed so its historical books stay readable.
calibration._rule_note: All three hardened checks enabled 2026-08-15 (advisor creative proposal #4). min_net_pnl = 0.0 states the thing the base three structurally cannot see: on 2026-08-14 control, gex and time_window all read qualified=true while lifetime-negative (-1,698.61 / -1,697.94 / -87.69), because a butterfly book wins often and loses big and a win-rate gate is blind to exactly that shape. min_return_on_capital = 0.0 and require_slippage_survival are NOT second profitability bars -- both are un-satisfiable while a reading carries no capital or no recorded slippage, and every flies arm today carries neither (capital_at_risk is null module-wide, slippage_coverage is 0 on every arm). Enabling them therefore states 'no flies arm may qualify until it is instrumented', deliberately: an arm certified on one real number and two absent ones is the failure this closes. Expect flies to qualify NOTHING until fly_positions records capital at risk and per-fill slippage -- that is the intended reading, not a regression.

calendars._comment: EXPERIMENTAL, off by default: switch on with modules.calendars.enabled once you have read its package README. Weekly SPX double-calendar paper module (packages/calendars): enters Mondays, holds through the week, so its loop runs Mon-Fri like everything else and self-gates entry to the entry day. Paper-only and credential-free -- no keyring_service, no broker_tool, no live block; its market data comes entirely from the shared stream cache via the streamer's `expirations` request field.

paper._tick_note: 30s resident: the per-tick mark path is the exit study's substrate, and its resolution bounds how precisely the read-side derivation can replay a trigger. Changing this cadence is a journaled measurement break in the module's own ledger.
paper._settlement_note: session_settled is today-scoped: it only reports false on a day this module has open legs expiring (the Friday shorts, the Monday longs), so the settlement check stays quiet the rest of the week. Grace 45: the module settles at 16:20 off a staleness-gated spot read and may retry for a while on a stale feed.

pmcc._comment: EXPERIMENTAL, off by default: switch on with modules.pmcc.enabled once you have read its package README. PMCC deep-ITM covered-call paper module (packages/pmcc): holds a ~1-year 0.90-0.95-delta call while a 0.70-delta weekly call rolls against it every Friday (the shield/shield_hold arms, the base trade since 2026-10-06), on XSP (cash-settled) and QQQ, GLD, IWM and SLV (physically settled); a position lives about ten months. Paper-only and credential-free -- no keyring_service, no broker_tool, no live block; market data comes entirely from the shared stream cache via the streamer's `expirations` and `window_hints` request fields.

paper._tick_note: 60s resident: the mark path feeds the tv-exhaustion trigger and the assignment-exposure telemetry, not a replay derivation, so it needs no calendars-grade resolution. Changing this cadence is a journaled measurement break in the module's own ledger.
paper._settlement_note: session_settled is today-scoped: it only reports false on a day this module has open legs expiring (a short's Friday, or the long's own expiry backstop). Grace 45: the module settles at 16:20 off a staleness-gated spot read and may retry for a while on a stale feed.

curve._comment: EXPERIMENTAL, off by default: switch on with modules.curve.enabled once you have read its package README. curve: VXX call credit spreads harvesting the VIX term-structure roll yield, gated by a daily VIX/VIX3M regime read (packages/curve). Paper-only and credential-free in the calendars/pmcc posture -- no keyring_service, no broker_tool, no live block; market data comes entirely from the shared stream cache. Note VXX is a real UNDERLYING here (a chain window plus its target expiration, ~700 subscriptions), unlike a quote-only leg: a new underlying needs a producer restart to pick up and trips the watchdog's subscription-growth recycle, so add it outside market hours and watch reconnect_count while it lands.

contango._comment: EXPERIMENTAL, off by default: switch on with modules.contango.enabled once you have read its package README. contango: the VIX/VIX3M regime switch held in shares (packages/contango) -- SVXY in contango, SHV (T-bills) otherwise, one decision per arm ten minutes before the close. Paper-only and credential-free: no keyring_service, no broker_tool, no live block. Its funds and VIX/VIX3M ride as quote-only stream legs, which the producer picks up on its next poll without a restart. It acts only inside its decision window, so it has no eval-activity reader (eval_activity.NOT_APPLICABLE); a missed window is on its own rows and in the review.

bwb._comment: SPX daily-laddered put broken-wing-butterfly module (packages/bwb): enters one BWB per enabled book every session at the expected move, ~7DTE, PM-settled; the books differ only in whether/when a reversal-triggered put credit spread add-on turns the fly into a 1-3-2. Paper by default and the paper loop is credential-free; market data comes entirely from the shared stream cache via the streamer's `expirations`/`window_hints` request fields. Since 2026-09-18 it also has a narrow LIVE path (one arm, per-day armed via /live-bwb-start, the full daily ladder under a worst-case cap, no closing orders) -- the keyring_service/broker_tool/live_db/live keys below are that path's, and the paper loop touches none of them.
bwb._broker_note: Live onboarding: `cherrypick connect/account --module bwb` drive broker_cli.py exactly like flies'. keyring service bwbagent (falls back to the shared suite login, so a box with that login needs no new secret); live_db is the SEPARATE live ledger read only by `report --live` (never by calibrate/promotion).
bwb._live_note: Watchdog + notification wiring for the module's LIVE loop (the module owns arming/trading; this block only tells the orchestrator how to WATCH it, and declaring task_name is what derives the bwb-live supervisor job from the arm record). The loop self-disarms at its own live.disarm_time; disarm_time/disarm_grace_minutes here are the watchdog's BACKSTOP window -- past it, a still-armed record means self-disarm failed, so the watchdog sets the suite halt flag and raises CRITICAL. notify_trades pushes live entries/add-ons/settlements from live_db with the LIVE prefix, from the notifier path (never the trading loop).

paper._tick_note: 60s resident: triggers are defined on the sampled series, not the continuous path, so this cadence is part of the measurement instrument -- changing it is a journaled measurement break, the flies 60s->15s precedent.
paper._fee_reconcile_note: Broker-cash reconciliation of settled LIVE expirations (2026-09-22), the same job flies runs. UNCONDITIONAL ON ARMING, which is the point: it used to ride the live tick, which runs only under --live on a job the supervisor disables the moment the loop disarms, so an expiration that settled on Tuesday went unconfirmed forever if Wednesday was never armed. 09:20 is after the broker posts the prior session's settlement lines and before the entry window opens. Needs the module's broker credentials (GET-only). Remove both keys to drop the job.
paper._settlement_note: session_settled is today-scoped: it only reports false on a day this module has open legs expiring (~7DTE PM-settled). Grace 45: the module settles at 16:20 off a staleness-gated spot read and may retry for a while on a stale feed.

paper._kind_note: self_healing since the 2026-08-12 lifecycle cutover, was cherrypick_scheduled. That kind registers exactly two daily jobs, an entry at entry_time and an exit at exit_time, which is the right shape for 'open one afternoon, close the next morning' and the wrong one for a position that is now MANAGED: a winner may be carried up to three sessions, a loser closes on the first reliable marks, and both need the book looked at every minute rather than twice a day. tick_interval_seconds is 60, so jobspec produces a single spawn-per-tick INTERVAL job (no resident process, MEIC's shape) -- the loop derives its own phase from the clock and no-ops outside the session, which is why it needs no window here. entry_time and entry_sla_grace_minutes are still read: the loop writes the same SLA heartbeats the scheduled verbs used to, so the watchdog's entry check and the dashboard cards are unchanged.
paper._entry_sla_note: OPTIONAL (default 35). Minutes past entry_time before the watchdog treats a missing entry heartbeat as CRITICAL. It is a grace, not a schedule: the entry scan starts inside the entry window, may run up to twenty-five minutes, and the heartbeat is only written when it RETURNS -- so comparing against entry_time alone raised CRITICAL for a run that was merely still in progress. Raise it if this module's entry scan legitimately runs longer.
paper._dolt_databases_note: Databases the runner needs served on dolt_host:dolt_port. doctor verifies each is present (not just that the port answers) when a MySQL client is available, catching a Dolt server rooted at the wrong data dir. Omit to check port reachability only.
paper._dolt_service_note: Optional cherrypick-managed keep-alive. `install` registers a MINUTE task that runs `ensure-dolt` (starts `dolt sql-server` from data_dir only when nothing is on the port); `uninstall` removes it; `status`/`doctor` surface it. data_dir is portable: `~` expands, a relative path resolves against the cherrypick runtime ROOT. Omit this block to manage Dolt yourself.

earnings._calibration_note: Earnings retired its conservative/balanced/aggressive risk-profile ladder; the strat_test paper book is now split per strategy (profile tag strat_test:<strategy>). With an empty ladder, calibrate reports per-book readings only (no promotion recommendation) -- strategies don't graduate rungs the way a risk ladder does.

watchdog._streamer_health_note: The dedicated STREAMER-ONLY liveness job: every interval_seconds across the whole session (start-end, ET, trading days), as its own supervisor job so the full 10-minute tick above never has to speed up to protect the streamer. Successor to the retired cherrypick-preopen windowed task (whose reasons all survive: a producer dead overnight must be caught before the unrecoverable 09:30-09:35 opening range, and a restart still needs the 240s settling window) with strictly broader coverage -- silence is now caught within ~5 min all session, not just pre-open. ON by default for the same reason preopen was.
watchdog._preopen_note: RETIRED (2026-08-09, supervisor cutover) -- replaced by streamer_health above. The block remains only so install/uninstall can delete the legacy cherrypick-preopen task by its resolved name; remove it once every machine has cut over.
watchdog._drawdown_note: Optional paper-P&L drift alert (net-of-cost). Add a 'drawdown' block to enable: {"suite_floor": -1000, "module_floors": {"meic": -750, "earnings": -750}, "critical_multiplier": 2}. net<=floor -> WARN; net<=floor*critical_multiplier -> CRITICAL. Paper only; never trades. Omit to disable.

_eval_activity_note: Eval-activity health for the continuous-loop modules (meic/flies): during RTH the watchdog + doctor read the module's eval log (MEIC loop_log, flies fly_snapshots) and confirm it is actually EVALUATING candidates and deciding sensibly, not just writing a file (freshness). Rejecting every candidate is HEALTHY (a legit gate, e.g. regime_gex_negative), so it WARNs only when: no evaluation for stale_minutes (stopped mid-session), iterating but evaluating nothing, >= error_fraction of evaluations erroring (e.g. a symbol with no price), or 0 entries for a reason that isn't a known gate. window_minutes is the lookback. Read-only; earnings is event-driven and covered by its entry-SLA check instead.

console._comment: The console (packages/console) is the suite's ONE read surface — every module's read models plus the scout research surfaces, on 127.0.0.1:5070. The supervisor keeps it up as an always-on RESIDENT job: no clock window and no trading-day gate, deliberately, since a read surface you can only open during RTH cannot be used to read the session that just ended. Its listen port lives in ~/.cherrypick/config/console.json ('serve.port'), not here. 'path' resolves like a module's (absolute, or relative to the orchestrator checkout); an unbuilt checkout reports the job disabled-with-a-reason rather than crash-looping — fix it with 'pnpm install && pnpm build' in packages/console.
console._silence_comment: Liveness is a heartbeat FILE (state/console.heartbeat), rewritten by the server every ~15s, not an HTTP probe: a Node event loop can wedge while the process stays alive and answering nothing, and the supervisor's reliability path stays free of network calls. Restart if the file goes untouched this long. Several heartbeats wide, so one slow pass is never read as a wedge.
console._dev_backoff_comment: Unset by default -- crashes back off up to the supervisor's normal 10-minute cap, same as every other job. Set dev_backoff_seconds (e.g. 20) only while actively iterating on packages/console, so a crash or a manual 'cherrypick restart-console' comes back in seconds instead of minutes. Remove it again once the checkout is stable.
console._reclaim_comment: ON by default. After 8 consecutive failed spawns (EADDRINUSE from something else holding the console's port), the supervisor checks who actually holds it; if that PID is not one it spawned or adopted, it kills that process tree and retries immediately instead of backing off forever. Recovers the 2026-08-23 incident automatically (an orphaned console child held :5070 for 9 hours / ~1600 failed restarts). Set false only if you deliberately want a manually-started console (e.g. 'pnpm dev:server') left alone indefinitely instead of reclaimed after ~3-4 minutes.

settings._comment: `cherrypick settings` — the local web editor for the suite's config files and keyring secrets. The suite's ONE mutating HTTP surface: loopback-only + per-session-token gated, run on demand in the foreground, never started by the watchdog or a scheduled task, and live-trading gate fields are read-only on it. Port 8804 is a fixed loopback slot, held over from the retired 88xx dashboard-embed range (those per-module dashboards were deleted at the 2026-08-12 console cutover; the console serves 5070).

streamer._comment: The suite's standalone market-data producer (packages/streamer) — the single streamer that writes the shared cache ~/.cherrypick/data/marketdata/stream_cache.db, which every module reads. THE sole producer since the 2026-07-21 cutover, and since 2026-10-18 the only one there is (MEIC's in-module rollback streamer was removed). Session-gated and silence-restarted by the watchdog. Located by 'path' (relative to this file). Modules declare which symbols they need via ~/.cherrypick/state/stream_requests/<module>.json — every module regenerates its own file on each run — and the streamer streams the union.
streamer._session_start_note: OPTIONAL, default 09:15 ET. When the watchdog starts the streamer on a trading day -- this check alone; every other session-gated check stays at 09:15. The watchdog ticks every interval_minutes, so the start lands up to one tick later. Not before the open is useful: equity options do not trade and the index level is static until 09:30, so the silence restart would loop.

services._comment: Long-running background daemons the orchestrator keeps alive: started at `install`, restarted by the watchdog if down (single-instance guarded), stopped at `uninstall`. Located by 'path' (relative to this file) or 'repo'. status_argv must print {"running": bool}. A running service whose config changed since launch is recycled (stop then start) so it re-reads -- the orchestrator stamps a hash of this entry plus the service's own config file at launch and compares each tick; requires auto_restart, and set 'config_name' if that config file is named for neither the checkout directory nor the id. The gex spot-trail recorder samples every symbol's spot continuously so the GEX dashboard's spot trail has no gaps and builds all session, independent of whether the dashboard is open. On by default: GEX is part of the base install (set enabled to false to turn the recorder off).

trade_notify._comment: Dedicated low-latency supervisor job that pushes new paper entries/exits to trade_channels. Runs far more often than the watchdog so fills reach you within ~30s instead of a full watchdog cycle. interval_seconds is the supervisor cadence (sub-minute became possible when the OS scheduler's 1-minute floor went away, 2026-08-09); a legacy interval_minutes is still honored if set explicitly. task_name is retained only so install/uninstall can delete the pre-supervisor task by name.

desk_notify._comment: Discord cards for MANUAL TRADING DESK orders (packages/desk), plus a fill watch. Posts a card when the desk submits an order and a second card when that order fills, cancels, is rejected, or expires. Reads the desk's append-only audit journal as a FILE and never imports cherrypick.desk - observing desk orders must never make the submit path reachable from scheduled code. It both calls the broker (read-only order status) and pushes a webhook, so it is its own scheduled job and is never called from the watchdog tick. OFF by default; set enabled=true, store the webhook (cherrypick secrets-set --channel discord), then re-run `install`.
desk_notify._watch_note: Fill detection is poll-first: the broker's order status is authoritative. The first pass after enabling SEEDS silently from the existing journal rather than backfilling a card for every order ever placed.
desk_notify._journal_path_note: Override the desk journal location. null uses the desk's own default, ~/.cherrypick/state/desk/journal.jsonl.
desk_notify._account_number_note: Which account to resolve for order-status lookups. null uses the default account for those credentials.

status_digest._comment: Hourly suite-status card to Discord: one field per module (closes, net, entry attempts, open risk, loop liveness) plus a header with the morning phase, watchdog verdict and the live halt flag. Composes existing artifacts only - it refreshes the provisional review fact set (the same idempotent build the 16:30 job runs) and reads it, watchdog.last.json and the morning pack; it never opens a module ledger itself. Pushes a webhook, so it is its own supervisor job and is never called from the watchdog tick. Two rendering rules are load-bearing: an unmeasured figure shows as an em dash (never $0), and no suite-wide net is ever printed (per-module nets only - see the review package's concentration rationale). OFF by default; set enabled=true, store the webhook (cherrypick secrets-set --channel discord), and the supervisor derives the job on its next pass.
status_digest._window_note: ET wall-clock, trading days only. 10:00 gives the first card a half-session to describe; 16:10 lets the ~16:00 fire land after the 0DTE modules settle.
status_digest._close_note: The one daily CLOSE card (status-digest-close job): same composition, posted after the 0DTE books settle and the official 16:30 review-provisional build, with deltas against the last hourly post.

flies_payoff_post._comment: Posts the flies 'payoff at expiry' chart to Discord once each ledger has settled: the console's payoff card for the session (captured by packages/console/tools/ui-check.mjs --card), captioned with each arm's settled net and the settlement print. Runs scripts/flies_payoff_post.py, never a package and never the watchdog tick. One post per ledger per session (state/flies-payoff-post.json); live waits for the official print. Needs the console up, node, and Chrome or Edge. OFF by default; set enabled=true and store the webhook (cherrypick secrets-set --channel discord).
flies_payoff_post._window_note: ET wall-clock, trading days only. Both ledgers settle at 16:20; each run posts whatever has settled and not been posted, so the window covers a late official print.

intraday._comment: The same chart while the book is still open, hourly through the session (job flies-payoff-intraday, scripts/flies_payoff_post.py --intraday), for the modes above. Captioned INTRADAY with each arm's open flies, net cash after fees, and the worst case at expiry with the band the floor holds over. One post per ledger per ET hour (state/flies-payoff-intraday.json); stands down once a ledger has settled. Independent of enabled above. OFF by default.
intraday._window_note: ET wall-clock, trading days only. 10:01 lands a minute after the status digest's hourly card; the last fire is 15:01.

notify._channels_note: Push channels are OFF by default: only 'log' (always on, the floor) is listed, and the console's own on-screen toasts need no setting. Add 'desktop' (Windows balloon, macOS notification centre, Linux notify-send), 'slack', 'discord' or 'telegram' to turn one on. push channels: 'log' (always on, the floor), 'desktop', 'slack', 'discord', 'telegram'. Slack/Discord webhook URLs live in the OS keyring (cherrypick secrets-set --channel slack|discord); Telegram needs a bot token and chat ID (cherrypick secrets-set --channel telegram). Never in this file or env vars.

trade_summary._mode_note: How MEIC trade events reach you: 'per-trade' (default) pushes each entry/stop/exit individually, with profile_prefixes below routing matching study arms to the digest; 'summary' routes EVERY MEIC trade to the periodic digest (one per-symbol roll-up every interval_minutes) and ignores profile_prefixes. Either way the digest is intraday-only: it pushes 09:15-17:00 ET on trading days (the tail covers the closing exits), and a flush due outside that window is held for the next in-window tick rather than dropped.
trade_summary._comment: MEIC risk_profile prefixes routed to a periodic per-symbol digest instead of a per-trade push (an uncapped sampling stream's 100+ trades/day would otherwise spam every entry/exit individually; built for the wing-width study, retired 2026-08-05, kept for every arm family since). Rows whose risk_profile starts with one of these prefixes are excluded from the normal per-trade lines. Updated 2026-08-07 for the arms cutover: `open`/`width-5`/`width-10` are the uncapped-sampling streams this exists for; `control` runs at book-like volume (overlap_scope 'shorts', capped concurrency) but is included for consistency, same as the old ladder names were. The retired ladder/GEX prefixes (conservative/moderate/aggressive/very-aggressive/gex-) are kept too — they still match any historical row from before the cutover.

review._comment: Cross-module end-of-day review (packages/review, `python -m cherrypick.review`) - the suite's one EOD answer since 2026-08-13, replacing the per-module EOD reports and the suite digest. Two scheduled passes per trading day because the modules do not all finish together: 'provisional_at' (ET, box-local clock) runs after the 0DTE modules settle - MEIC and flies complete, earnings shown as carried overnight risk - and 'final_at' the next morning finalises the PRIOR session once earnings' 09:45 close window has run. Each pass writes one versioned fact set (data/review/eod-<day>.json) plus its render; read-only over every module's ledger, writes only into review's own home, so a failed pass costs a report, never a trade. ON by default; opt out with enabled=false then re-run `install`. 'narrative' (OFF by default) schedules the agent-written note at 'narrative_at', after the final pass so it only ever sees a finalised session - it shells out to Claude Code (`claude` on PATH), a dependency the suite does not otherwise have, and the note is written BESIDE the facts, never inside them, so a failed note cannot damage the record. 'file_issues' additionally lets that narrative run file its recommendations as tracked GitHub issues (needs `gh`; deduped and capped per run).

manage._comment: Daily position-management evaluation of the REAL broker account (packages/manage, `run.py manage`). At 'at' (ET) on trading days the orchestrator reads the account read-only - priced positions and balances (the `positions` verb) plus each underlying's last price, earnings and ex-dividend dates - and packages/manage judges every trade against its ruleset (credit: take profit at 50%, stop at a loss equal to the credit, 21 DTE; debit: stop at -50%, take profit at +75%; never hold a physically-settled option into expiry; never roll a loser). The evaluation lands in data/manage/eval-<day>.json and on the console's Live page. Advice only: nothing places, closes or sizes an order. The ruleset is manage's own config, ~/.cherrypick/config/manage.json (see packages/manage/config.example.json; keep only what you change). OFF by default because it reads the live account daily; 'also_at' lists further ET times the same day (each its own `manage-eval-HHMM` job, rewriting the day's evaluation - one after the close leaves the day's last word); 'notify' posts the trades needing action, one line each, after every run. Re-run `install` after turning it on.
manage._roll_out_note: The quoted expiries the snapshot carries past each short a roll would move out in time: a covered call, a PMCC's short and a short put (no long put on the name), each within 'max_short_days' of expiry. One read per expiry per name (plus one listing per name when the stream cache does not hold it): the next 'expiries', before the long's expiry for a PMCC and within 'max_days' of the short's otherwise, each quoted 40 strikes either side of the short's strike. 'max_calls' and 'max_seconds' cap the step; what they cut is recorded in the snapshot, never fatal.

morning._comment: Pre-open market overview (packages/overview, `python -m cherrypick.overview`) - the morning sibling of the review. One scheduled pass per trading day at 'factpack_at' (ET, box-local clock) builds a deterministic fact pack (data/overview/morning-<day>.json) plus its render: index/vol/sector readings from the shared stream cache (prior-session values labeled prior, live pre-open quotes labeled live), gamma flip and walls from the suite's own GEX history, and a mechanical GREEN/YELLOW/RED phase computed from five declared gates - missing data can never produce RED and always blocks GREEN. Pure stream-cache + GEX consumer: no credential, no network, writes only into overview's own home, so a failed pass costs a report, never a trade. The pack's breadth symbols (VIX/VIX3M/VVIX, sector ETFs, USO/GLD proxies) are declared via state/stream_requests/overview.json; the FIRST build registers them, and the streamer picks them up on its next producer recycle. ON by default; opt out with enabled=false then re-run `install`. 'narrative' (OFF by default) schedules the agent-written morning note at 'narrative_at' via scripts/morning_narrative.py - it shells out to Claude Code (`claude` on PATH) and, unlike the EOD narrative, is allowed web lookups for the macro calendar; market numbers still come only from the pack, and the note is written BESIDE the facts, never inside them.
morning._comment_files: The daily market files the pack reads (scripts/fetch_market_files.py): Cboe's SKEW/VIX/VVIX/VXN histories, Treasury's par yield curve, BEA's release dates, and OCC's daily option volume by underlying with Nasdaq Trader's symbol directory (the pack's hot options; OCC posts a session around 23:15 ET, so the 'files_retry_at' run is the one that lands it; each run lands any of the last 25 it lacks), into data/market-files/. Credential-free, so ON with the pack: 'files_at' after Treasury posts (~18:00 ET), 'files_retry_at' before the pack builds. A download that parses to less than the file on disk is refused, so a failed fetch leaves yesterday's files. CPI, jobs and PPI dates need a free FRED API key, stored once with `python scripts/fetch_market_files.py fred-key`; without one the calendar carries BEA's releases and the FOMC dates only.
morning._comment_earnings_moves: Next week's earnings among the stocks the market report covers, each with the move its post-event straddle implies (scripts/fetch_earnings_moves.py; 0.85 x the ATM straddle, the suite's one definition), priced at the close into data/market-report/earnings/week.json for the next morning's pack. Reads the shared broker credential, read-only, one chain a second.
morning._comment_headlines: The morning's headlines for the narrative (scripts/fetch_headlines.py): titles, links, sources and times from the Fed, CNBC, MarketWatch and WSJ RSS feeds, one request each, into data/market-report/headlines/<date>.json. No article bodies. Only scripts/morning_narrative.py reads it.

technicals._comment: packages/technicals - the market report's end-of-day store. Lands raw daily bars, splits, dividends and IV history for the universe candidates, the 35 rotation ETFs and the benchmarks from the LOCAL Dolt clones into data/technicals/eod.db, at 'land_at' ET after the 05:30 Dolt pull. Adjusted bars are computed from raw on read. Read-only against Dolt; needs the earnings module on, since its job keeps the dolt sql-server alive. ON by default.
technicals._comment_stage_lists_at: Our six stage lists (python -m cherrypick.technicals stage-lists, local data only): the stage rule on the close the landing just added, options-tradable names only, in technicals/stage-lists/<session>.json, scored against the vendor's saved watchlists while they exist. Mirror them to tastytrade by hand with python scripts/sync_stage_watchlists.py --apply. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_history_at: The history store's daily top-up from the local Dolt clones (python -m cherrypick.technicals history land at history_at, every listed name's raw bars, ~20 s; history fundamentals at fundamentals_at, the weekly estimate snapshots and quarterly statements, ~10 s). Incremental and read-only against Dolt. The signal board's fundamentals score reads it. ET.
technicals._comment_board_at: The signal board (python -m cherrypick.technicals board, local data only): each listed stock's count of methods agreeing on one side -- RS stage, its sector's rotation, fundamentals (our score's market tails), the trend scan and that session's analyst revisions -- for the console's Screeners signal board. After report_at and the history top-up, with the previous evening's revisions fetch. Record-only. ET.
technicals._comment_dividends: scripts/fetch_dividends.py: tastytrade's dividend history, which the landing reconciles Dolt's against (Dolt alone has gaps and zeros; reconciled, adjusted bars match the vendor's on 36 of 40 names). Reads the shared broker credential, read-only, one symbol a second, refetching only symbols older than a week.
technicals._comment_iv_rank: scripts/fetch_iv_rank.py: tastytrade's IV rank (and liquidity rating) for every stored name, one reading per session. The technicals store ranks Dolt's IV itself and falls back to this where Dolt has no IV for a name. Reads the shared broker credential, read-only, 50 symbols a request. Trading days, after the close.
technicals._comment_dollar_volume: scripts/fetch_dollar_volume.py: every optionable name's 50-session median dollar volume (close x volume) from tastytrade's daily candles, extended hours (the consolidated volume; the regular-hours candle is a fraction of it), ~140 s for ~5,600 names. The security list's liquidity rank and the liquidity verdict read it. Needs no Dolt: it runs whenever this block is on, even where the Dolt-reading jobs are off. Trading days, ET, before the 18:48 security list.
technicals._comment_earnings_times_at: The earnings calendar's third time-of-day source (scripts/fetch_earnings_times.py): before or after the open for every announcement in the next month, from Nasdaq's public calendar -- network, no credential, one request per date two seconds apart, stopping at a 403 or 429. It agreed with the broker and Dolt on all 378 names they timed on 2026-10-17. Before earnings_calendar_at. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_sectors_at: The earnings calendar's second sector source (scripts/fetch_sectors.py): Yahoo's sector, relabelled to the vendor's names, for the calendar names the vendor's sector map lacks -- network, no credential, one search request per name half a second apart, stopping at a 403 or 429. A name is asked again after six months (a month if Yahoo had none). It agreed with the vendor's sector on all 120 names sampled on 2026-10-17. Before earnings_calendar_at. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_revisions_at: Analyst revisions (scripts/fetch_analyst_revisions.py): Yahoo's per-firm rating and price-target history for every name the technicals store lands and every name on the latest income screener lists (~1,020), appended to market-report/analysts/revisions.db so it stays point-in-time; packages/technicals reads it (revisions.py, score-revisions). Network, no credential, one request per name two seconds apart (~35 minutes), stopping at a 429. After the session's notes are out. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_adjust_check: The corporate-action tripwire (2026-10-27; the vendor's chart captures that did this stopped on 10-23). scripts/fetch_yahoo_adjusted.py reads a year of Yahoo's adjusted closes for every stored name at yahoo_adjusted_at into market-report/adjusted/yahoo.db -- network, no credential, one request per name 0.6 s apart, stopping at a 403 or 429. python -m cherrypick.technicals check-adjust compares our adjusted bars with them at adjust_check_at, after the landing, and exits non-zero on a step in the ratio of the two that no declared reason covers (a split, spin-off or dividend one side lacks). Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_liquidity_at: The nightly liquidity verdict (python -m cherrypick.technicals liquidity, local data only): a name failing the options-tradable test (weekly options, $100M a day) is held illiquid until the monthly sweep on the first trading day of the month. Broker-spending scripts skip it and listed views hide it; its bars and every count keep it. After iv_rank_at, before the 19:00 screener greeks run. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_securities_at: The public security list (python -m cherrypick.technicals securities, local files only): every listed symbol's type from Nasdaq Trader's directory, options from OCC's volume, and our own liquidity rank (option and stock dollar volume), plus market-report/securities/current.json naming which list the readers use -- the vendor's while market_report.collector is on and its list is at most four days old, else this one. After the 18:45 market-files run, before iv_rank_at. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_income_lists_at: Our own short-put and covered-call lists (python -m cherrypick.technicals income-lists, local files only): the put nearest 16 delta on the cycle monthly and the call nearest 16 delta on the monthly 30-45 days out, from the 14:45 income chains, at the working price. The Screeners page's short puts and covered calls tabs read them. No Dolt needed; off when market_report.income is. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_screeners_at: Score the income screens' expiry and strike rules (python -m cherrypick.technicals score-screeners, local files only) against every saved screener list that has its broker chain; a session already scored is skipped. In the morning, after the previous evening's late greeks run. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_skate: The skate screen's range bands (python -m cherrypick.technicals skate, the history store and local files only, ~90 s): for every options-tradable name, side and weekly expiry to 63 days, the fixed and by-expiry bands and how often each held since 2015 (docs/skate-plan.md). Needs technicals.history. Trading days, ET, after the 06:20 history top-up.
technicals._comment_earnings_calendar_at: The earnings calendar (python -m cherrypick.technicals earnings-calendar, local data and the local Dolt only): every announcement in the next 30 days with our direction and strength (from the store's bars), the broker's IV rank, and the broker's expected move (0.85 x the ATM straddle) from the IV-rank fetch's per-expiration IVs, for the console's earnings tab (docs/earnings-screener-plan.md). After iv_rank_at and the 17:15 chart run; the late pass catches a security list saved after the first. A rerun replaces the session's file. Trading days, ET.
technicals._comment_earnings_record_at: The earnings calendar's forward record (python -m cherrypick.technicals earnings-record, local files and the local Dolt): each past announcement's move against the one-SD move the calendar showed the session before, whether a strong read called it, and the suggested spread entered on its entry session's last reading and marked on the reaction day and the next. Rebuilt whole each morning, after the 05:30 Dolt pull. Trading days, ET.

live_positions._comment: run.py live-positions, every interval_seconds from start to end ET on trading days: each designated live account's broker positions (read-only get_positions) against what the flies/bwb/meic live ledgers say is filled and open, on the underlyings those modules trade. Asks the broker only while a live module is armed or holds a ledger leg. A difference seen on two checks running is a CRITICAL watchdog finding (live_positions); contracts already expired are left out, since the broker lists them until its overnight processing. Safeguard 2(c), 2026-10-08.

live_settle_overdue._comment: run.py settle-overdue-live, every interval_seconds, every day: settles any past session a flies, bwb or meic live ledger still holds open (a machine down between the close and the disarm) at THAT session's official close (Yahoo daily bar, source yahoo_daily) -- never a provisional price. A session with a pending entry, or no official close found, stays open and the watchdog keeps alerting. Each settlement is announced on every channel. Safeguard item 4, 2026-10-08 (the owner chose official-print-only).

service._comment: OPTIONAL Windows-service mode (run.py service): the supervisor as a WinSW v2 service, so the suite runs with nobody logged on. Off by default -- the default posture is auto-logon plus the logged-on anchor task. To use: download WinSW-x64.exe (v2.x, github.com/winsw/winsw/releases), set winsw_exe to its path and enabled to true, run `run.py service prepare`, then the printed commands in an administrator prompt. The service runs as you (Credential Manager stays readable); its password is asked for at install and stored by Windows, never in a file.

power_watch._comment: run.py power-watch, every 60 s, every day: while this machine runs on battery, notify ALL channels (log, desktop, discord, slack -- any without a webhook is skipped) the moment it switches and every repeat_minutes, WARNING turning CRITICAL at critical_percent charge or critical_minutes of estimated time left; one message when AC returns. Reads Windows (GetSystemPowerStatus), Linux (/sys/class/power_supply; a machine with no battery entry never alerts) and macOS (pmset -g batt); a reading it cannot take stays quiet. Added after the 2026-10-08 power outage ran the laptop down mid-session.

backtest._comment: The nightly vendor fetch for packages/backtest (job backtest-fetch, `python -m cherrypick.backtest fetch --cadence <fetch_cadence> --recent <fetch_recent_sessions>`). OFF by default: it needs a vendor subscription, the key in the keyring (python -m cherrypick.backtest key set) and ~/.cherrypick/config/backtest.json enabled, plus the vendor library (pip install -e "packages/backtest[thetadata]"). Trading days only at fetch_at (ET); complete sessions are skipped, so a missed night is picked up by the next. While it runs it holds the vendor account's only session: do not log in with the key elsewhere then.

research_queue._comment: The research queue (job research-queue, `run.py queue-run`; orchestrator/researchqueue.py): long research tasks added as rows with `run.py queue-add --study <study> [--step <step>] --task <kind> --task-args <json> [--output <file>]`, each named study/step (lowercase slugs; the study is its category; one live row per name; a finished row points to its counts, input or declared output, and log), run one at a time by the supervisor, so a many-hour fetch survives the terminal or assistant session that queued it. Allow-listed kinds only: fetch-chains, fetch-flow (resumable ThetaData fetches, bounded by --stop-by) and script (a file checked into scripts/, string arguments, no shell). A ThetaData task waits while the vendor session is held and keeps clear of the nightly backtest-fetch, from blackout_before_minutes before backtest.fetch_at to blackout_after_minutes after on trading days: it stops there and resumes after. One notification per finished or failed task. On by default: with no rows it does nothing. `run.py queue-list` shows the rows and why a queued one waits.

quikoptions._comment: QuikOptions' Hot Options Report (scripts/fetch_quikoptions.py; docs/quikoptions-plan.md): one paced load a day after the close in the installed Chrome, on a profile a person signs in to by hand, then the economic calendar through the menu. Kept only when the page's own sums hold, into data/quikoptions/. 'enabled' also shows the console's Options flow page. A 429, or a 403 once signed in, starts a 24-hour cooldown; an expired session notifies and stops. OFF by default: sign in first (`python scripts/fetch_quikoptions.py login`), then set enabled=true. Scheduled, trading days only: the capture at 'at' (plus 0-jitter_minutes), scoring at score_at, and the next morning the open-interest confirmation at confirm_at; each later step waits up to 45 minutes for the one before it. 'headed' runs the capture in a visible browser (off: headless, the default) -- for a session a person is watching for errors. You are responsible for complying with the site's terms. Times are ET.
quikoptions._comment_post: The daily Discord series: the Options flow cards named in post_cards as screen captures, each under its own title, the first also under the series title line. OFF by default and needs enabled: it republishes the site's figures, so re-read their terms for redistribution first. post_webhook: 'reporting' (the reporting channel, cherrypick secrets-set --channel discord_reporting; 'dedicated' still works) or 'notify' (the suite's Discord notify webhook); a choice, never a fallback. post_cards, from: Derived flow, Net by name, Trades (the site's Birdseye; the old name still works), Names across tables, Largest by contracts, Top sweeps, Top spreads, Vol / OI. post_title heads the first picture (one line, at most 80 characters); the session date is always added after it.
quikoptions._comment_post_style: post_style: 'singles' (the default, chosen 2026-10-03: each card as its own titled screen capture, the first under the series title, readable on a phone), 'text' (plain text tables), 'cards' (a header embed, then the cards as images two to a message), or 'embed' (one embed of small tables, no images). post_cards may also name 'Events': the session's high-impact releases with actual against estimate, and the next ones.
quikoptions._comment_post_followups: post_morning: after the open-interest check, how the last session's flows came out (opened, closed, mixed). post_weekly: Friday's scorecard (the week's checks, confirmations, and how the calls did a day on; descriptive only until the fixed 40-session test), on the week's last trading day, and always to the suite's Discord notify webhook, never the reporting channel, whatever post_webhook says. Both narrow text, both need post.

market_report._comment: The vendor-edition collector (scripts/fetch_vendor_edition.py) - the fixture feed for docs/market-report-plan.md. Fetches the vendor's pre-open report after it is published ('edition_at', with a second chance at 'edition_retry_at'; a day already saved is skipped) and, after the close, the data behind its chart pages ('charts_at'), into data/market-report/. Paced on purpose: one browser session, 20-60 s between pages, at most 40 chart pages, and a 24-hour cooldown after any 429/403. Stops at a captcha or refused login and notifies. OFF by default: store the login first (`python scripts/fetch_vendor_edition.py credentials` then `login`), put the dashboard address in data/market-report/collector.json, then set collector=true and re-run `install`. Times are ET.
market_report._vendor_note: The collector needs both of these, and does not run without them even with collector true. vendor_dashboard_url: the address of the subscription dashboard the edition is read from. vendor_edition_title: the title the report carries before its date ('<title> - September 25, 2026'). The login itself is in the OS keyring (python scripts/fetch_vendor_edition.py credentials). You are responsible for complying with that service's terms.
market_report._comment_universe: The stock-universe builder (scripts/build_stock_universe.py): candidates from every saved vendor edition and the tastylive follow feed, kept only when measured very liquid: tight stock and ATM option spreads from tastytrade REST quotes, and at least 10,000 option contracts a day from OCC's daily volume file, each a median over at least 3 sessions. tastytrade's liquidity rating is recorded as a guide and never decides. 'universe_measure_at' are two regular-hours measurements (the script refuses outside 10:00 ET to 30 minutes before the close); 'universe_daily_at' harvests and rebuilds data/market-report/universe/universe.json. Read-only against the broker. OFF by default: it reads the shared tastytrade credential. Times are ET.
market_report._comment_universe_watchlist: Mirror the universe's members to a private tastytrade watchlist named 'cherrypick universe' (scripts/build_stock_universe.py watchlist --apply) at 'universe_watchlist_at', after the daily rebuild. The suite's one scheduled write to the broker account - a watchlist, never an order - so it is its own switch, OFF by default even with universe=true. SPX, NDX, SPY, QQQ and IWM are pinned to the list and never removed. It only replaces the list it created (group 'cherrypick'), and refuses to strip the list to its pins or remove more than half of the universe's names in one sync. Preview any time with `python scripts/build_stock_universe.py watchlist`.
market_report._comment_screener_greeks: Record the broker's option chain around every row of the evening's income screener lists (scripts/fetch_screener_greeks.py): every listed strike for the row's expiry, and delta, IV, bid/ask and open interest for the strikes around the vendor's. The input for re-creating the vendor's screen from broker data. Writes data/market-report/screener-greeks/<date>.json at 'screener_greeks_at', after the chart capture that saves the lists. Read-only against the broker. OFF by default: it reads the shared tastytrade credential. Times are ET.
market_report._comment_screener_greeks_late_at: With screener_greeks on: the night's second, last run, for a chart capture that landed after screener_greeks_at. It records today's lists if they have come since, does nothing if the evening run already did, and fails (a failed-job alert) if today's lists were never saved, since the broker chain cannot be recorded for a past day. Before midnight ET, with its catch-up. Times are ET.
market_report._comment_earnings_strikes_at: With screener_greeks on: the earnings calendar's suggested spreads matched to listed strikes (scripts/fetch_screener_greeks.py strikes) -- the chain listing of each strong read reporting within the week, after the 19:10 calendar build, so the earnings tab shows real strikes rather than target prices until the next regular-hours reading prices them. Listings only, read-only, a second a name. Times are ET.
market_report._comment_income: Every tradable name's cycle-monthly chain (45-60 DTE, else 30-60), out of the money both sides, and the covered call's own monthly 30-45 days out, quoted in regular hours at income_chains_at (fetch_screener_greeks.py income). The Screeners page's short-put and covered-call lists and manage's income candidates read it; no vendor list needed. Reads the shared broker credential, read-only. On by default.
market_report._comment_screener_measure_at: With screener_greeks on: two regular-hours readings (fetch_screener_greeks.py measure) of the ATM monthly call and put spread for every listed name the universe builder does not already measure. After-hours quotes say nothing about a name's spread. Half an hour after the universe's own readings, inside the same 10:00-to-30-minutes-before-the-close window. Times are ET.
market_report._comment_skate_quotes_at: With screener_greeks on and technicals.skate on: two regular-hours passes (fetch_screener_greeks.py skate) quoting the skate screen's strikes past the morning's range bands and scoring them -- every name-side on its cycle monthly, then every weekly to 63 days for the name-sides whose history beats their implied odds by the most (docs/skate-plan.md). The first pass of a day lists the chains, about six minutes; the second reuses them. Read-only. Times are ET.

data_epoch._comment: Optional restatement marker. Declare when a correctness fix RESTATES what recorded paper history means (e.g. the phase-0 leg-ratio / fee-count / win-definition fixes): set 'date' to the first session traded on fixed code. `report` stays descriptive (totals still cover all history, plus a pre_epoch_trades count per module); `calibrate` ENFORCES it - promotion readings use only sessions on/after the date, so a rung can never graduate on numbers produced by retired code. Remove or leave date null when no restatement is in effect.

log_archive._comment: End-of-month log/report rotation (`cherrypick archive`). A monthly scheduled task zips each FINISHED month's dated reports (paper-eod / eod-analysis / eod-digest / live eod) and rotated log backups (*.log.N) into logs/archive/<YYYY-MM>/<scope>.zip - one zip per scope (the suite logs root + each module dir) - then removes the originals once the zip verifies. Idempotent and safe: it never touches the current month or an active .log, and re-runs converge. ON by default and registered by `install`; OPT OUT with enabled=false then re-run `install`/`uninstall`. 'day' is the day of month it fires (1..28), 'at' the box's local clock. Files only; off the watchdog reliability path. Run on demand any time with `cherrypick archive` (add --dry-run to preview, --month YYYY-MM to scope to one month).

config_backup._comment: A git history of this machine's configuration, OFF by default. `run.py config-backup --init [--remote <url>]` makes ~/.cherrypick a git repository whose .gitignore admits only config.json and config/*.json (never data, state, logs or credentials); then every interval_minutes the config-backup job commits what changed and, with push, pushes to the remote. Switch on here, on the console's Config page, or with `run.py config-backup --enable`. Use a PRIVATE remote: the files hold your strategy settings.

backup._comment: The nightly suite backup (orchestrator.backup, the suite-backup job; run by hand with `cherrypick backup`). One verified zip of the suite's own data -- configs, state, every ledger (copied through SQLite's online backup API and quick_checked) and every artifact under data/ -- written to dest/cherrypick-backup.zip and REPLACED each night; only the latest is kept. A night with a problem never overwrites the good one (it lands as cherrypick-backup.failed.zip and notifies). Not included: the Dolt stores (re-pullable), the stream caches, logs, the vendor browser profile, and backup/archive copies. dest defaults to ~/.cherrypick/backups, the same disk: set it to another drive or a synced folder to survive a lost disk. `at` is ET.

advisor._comment: The AI advisor (packages/advisor + scripts/advisor_checkpoint.py) - agent advises, loop decides. Eight scheduled slots per trading day: seven light intraday checkpoints ('checkpoints', ET) on 'light_model' that observe and draft, and one deep post-close run ('deep_at', after review-provisional at 16:30) on 'deep_model' that designs experiments, passes verdicts, and issues the NEXT session's advice. Each run builds a deterministic fact pack in-package, pipes it to Claude headless on stdin with ALL acting tools denied, and hands the reply back to the package to validate - the AI never gets a file handle, a database, or a tool. Admitted proposals run as paper A/B experiments: one synthetic 'advised:<experiment name>' book per experiment beside its un-advised control, scored by the same qualification gate everything else uses. The artifact is state/advice/<module>-<session>.json, validated by cherrypick.core.advice and re-validated by the loop at session start; absent/stale/invalid means baseline, and one out-of-bounds value rejects the whole set (rejections are still written, for audit). OFF by default TWICE: 'enabled' here AND the module's OWN 'advice' block (in ~/.cherrypick/config/<module>.json), which is where the bounds manifest now lives - the module declares what it will accept advice about, not this file. Kill switch: flip either flag, delete the advice file, or `python -m cherrypick.advisor kill <experiment_id>`. Paper only: nothing here can reach a live account, and the deep slot's enact step runs even when the AI call fails so an outage cannot truncate an active A/B sample. 'max_experiments_per_module' is null = unlimited (2026-09-17, was 1): each consumer builds one advised book PER EXPERIMENT, advised:<experiment name>, so any number run side by side against the same control; a number caps the module's advised roster and over-cap specs queue and activate FIFO. 'experiment_sessions' defaults to 15 so an expiring experiment can satisfy the promotion gate (14 days, 20 trades) instead of expiring underpowered.
advisor._checkpoints_note: Light intraday checkpoints. EMPTY since 2026-08-26: the schedule is the deep post-close run and nothing else. Seven light slots ran from 08-14, were cut to one on 08-21 and to none on 08-26, on the advisor's own record rather than on preference - across 36 light checkpoints they produced four 'creative' proposals (the kind no code path acts on), zero experiment_spec/tune/verdict, and one critical flag that the same evening's deep slot re-derived more precisely from settled numbers. 'midday', the last one standing, produced zero proposals in its entire history. They also cannot ISSUE anything: the only loop-facing output is the artifact the deep slot's enact step writes for the next session. And they cost the deep slot ~43KB, about 10% of the pack it has to read. What they were nominally for - a dropped advice artifact visible at 10am rather than in the evening verdict - is deterministic and is now the watchdog's advisor.enactment check, which invokes 'python -m cherrypick.advisor enactment' by subprocess between 10:30 and 16:30. Light slots remain fully supported: populate this to bring them back, as a LIST of times (named positionally from ADVISOR_LIGHT_SLOTS) or a DICT of {slot_name: time} when you want fewer than seven and legible names.

reconcile._comment: `cherrypick reconcile` (and the serve-only /api/reconcile dashboard card): a paper<->live isolation guard. It enumerates EVERY account on the login (list_accounts - tastytrade returns multiple per user) and checks each (read-only get_positions/get_account_info), flagging any open positions/BP a paper-only suite shouldn't have. On-demand and off the watchdog reliability path; never trades; account numbers masked. Optional 'broker_module' forces which module's tt.py to query; omit to auto-discover the first positions-capable one.

schedule._comment: Phase-5 posture: once any module trades live, reconcile stops being on-demand-only and runs daily as its own scheduled task ('at' in market-timezone HH:MM, after the close). The task runs `reconcile --scheduled`, which pushes a notification on any non-FLAT verdict (DRIFT -> CRITICAL, UNKNOWN -> WARNING) and stays quiet when flat. Its own task, deliberately OFF the watchdog tick - the broker call never rides the reliability path. Off by default; enable then re-run `install`.

symbol_watch._comment: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-12 and must stay OFF. The earnings module now runs this scan itself, as the `forward_scan` phase of its own 60-second loop (`symbol_watch.enabled`/`at`/`days` in the EARNINGS config), because it feeds that module's entry pre-filter as well as the console's Upcoming surface -- and a scan whose output gates an entry belongs on the same clock as the entry. Enabling this block would run the same scan a second time: harmless to the data (the snapshot is rewritten wholesale) but a wasted multi-minute broker walk. Kept derivable only so an existing install that had it enabled keeps working until its config is updated.
